description_full: THOR Industries, Inc. manufactures and sells recreational vehicles (RVs), and related parts and accessories in the United States, Germany, rest of Europe, Canada, and internationally. It operates through three segments: North American Towable Recreational Vehicles; North American Motorized Recreational Vehicles; and European Recreational Vehicles. The company offers travel trailers and motorhomes; Class A, Class C and Class B motorhomes; and fifth wheels under the Airstream Classic, Globetrotter, International, Tradewind, Flying Cloud, Caravel, Bambi, World Traveler, Basecamp, Interstate, Atlas, Rangeline, Jay Flight, Jay Feather, Eagle, Pinnacle, Colt, Range Lite, 3X, Prowler, North Trail, Big Horn, Odyssey, Esteem, Emblem, Insignia, Montana, Springdale, Hideout, Sprinter, Arcadia, Bullet, Fuzion, Raptor, Reign, Passport, Sprout, Cougar, Coleman, Kodiak, Aspen Trail, Astoria, Voltage, Colorado, Sunset Trail, Zinger, Redwood, Classic, Sportsmen, Connect, Ridgeway, Durango, Durango Gold, Sportster X, Sienna, Sonic, Stratus, and SportTrek brands. It also provides gasoline and diesel Class A products under the ACE, Resonate, Hurricane, Windsport, Outlaw, Indigo, Luminate, Vegas, Axis, Rize, Scope, Sequence, Tellaro, Palladium, Talavera, Sanctuary, Tranquility, Four Winds, Chateau, Compass, Gemini, Magnitude, Omni, Inception, Pasadena, Inception HD, Pasadena SV, Palazzo, Riviera, Aria, Allegro, Allegro Bay, Allegro Breeze, Allegro Bus, Allegro Red, Byway, GH1, GH2, GT1, GT2, Midas, Open Trail, Phaeton, Wayfarer, and Zephyr. In addition, the company offers recreational vehicles; and motorized and towable recreational vehicles, including motorcaravans, campervans, urban vehicles, and caravan. Further, it sells RV-related products; and manufactures and sells aluminum extrusions and specialized component products. The company sells its products to independent and non-franchise dealers. THOR Industries, Inc. was founded in 1980 and is based in Elkhart, Indiana.

financial_summary: Thor Industries, Inc. is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $4.0B market cap on $9.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -5% over the past three years and +8% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 6% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 14% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $169M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.81× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 5.3×.

Management returns a meaningful 5.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 4.9% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
